1.1.26.en: Fixed hybrid (energy storage) systems showing no values at all — every poll failed on fields that don't exist in the storage data. Power, Lifetime Energy and battery level now update; the battery level is a true average across inverters. Removed the Daily Energy tile on hybrids, which never had a value (the storage data has no daily field). Pairing now refuses a hybrid gateway whose inverter list can't be read, instead of adding a device that never updates. Added a "Restore capabilities" button (device settings → Maintenance) that re-adds missing tiles with their correct names — no re-pairing, Flows and Insights are kept. Changing Panel Count or Three-phase in the settings now adds the matching tiles right away. The panel count is no longer lowered on restart, which froze some panel tiles. Fixed yesterday's Daily Energy showing in the early morning for locations east of UTC+5 (e.g. Asia, Australia). Changing Solar latitude/longitude now takes effect right away instead of the next day. New optional "Nominal power (W)" setting: when set, adds a Power Ratio (%) tile (current power ÷ nominal power), handy for Flows such as "production below 10%". Repair: a new DTU IP address now takes effect immediately (it used to wait up to 20 minutes for an automatic reconnect). Fixed: device Flow triggers (solar production started/stopped, daily data updated, data updated, fault detected) never fired. "Solar production started" now needs more than 25 W (it fired at dawn on 5 W), and "stopped" needs three low readings in a row, so a single 0 W reading from the DTU mid-day no longer fires stopped + started; at night "stopped" and the daily summary also fire when the inverter falls asleep first. New device setting "Debug logging": when asked for a diagnostic report, turn it on for the DTU with the problem — it logs every poll and request for that DTU only (never the Wi-Fi password or encryption keys) and switches itself off after 60 minutes.

1.0.0.en: Rewritten in Python using the official hoymiles-wifi library. Improved support for DTU-WLite, DTU-Pro, and DTU-Pro-S. Auto-detection of panel count, three-phase, hybrid, and encrypted inverters. No cloud required.

1.1.1.en: Rewritten in Python using the official hoymiles-wifi library. Full support for DTU-WLite, DTU-Pro, and DTU-Pro-S (encrypted). Auto-detection of panel count, three-phase, hybrid, and encrypted inverters. Automatic night-time detection — device stays available overnight. No cloud required.

1.1.2.en: Rewritten in Python using the official hoymiles-wifi library. Full support for DTU-WLite, DTU-Pro, and DTU-Pro-S (encrypted). Auto-detection of panel count, three-phase, hybrid, and encrypted inverters. Automatic night-time detection — device stays available overnight. No cloud required.

1.1.3.en: Added support for 10 languages: Dutch, German, French, Italian, Swedish, Norwegian, Spanish, Danish, and Polish.

1.1.6.en: Fix pairing crash: replace self.homey.__() with self.homey.translate()

1.1.7.en: Fixed: pairing crash — "Homey object has no attribute '__'" error when DTU cannot be reached

1.1.9.en: Added confirmation step during pairing to review and correct auto-detected DTU structure before creating capabilities. Added repair flow to update DTU IP and encryption settings without re-pairing. Multiple DTUs can now be added in a single pairing session. Fixed: night-time detection now correctly disabled when Homey geolocation is unavailable. Fixed: panel data mapped by enumeration index instead of port number, preventing missing panel readings.

1.1.10.en: Improved pairing flow: automatic network scan first, with manual IP fallback only when discovery fails. Multiple DTUs can be found and added in a single flow. Removed the repair flow. Optimized sun time calculation by caching sunrise and sunset once per day.

1.1.11.en: Improved pairing flow: automatic network scan first, with manual IP fallback only when discovery fails. Multiple DTUs can be found and added in a single flow. Removed the repair flow. Optimized sun time calculation by caching sunrise and sunset once per day.

1.1.12.en: Fixed: pairing no longer asks for panel count when auto-detection is confident (live inverter data). Fixed: total power (W) and daily energy (kWh) on the main device card now show correct values on DTUs that report zero at the DTU level (e.g. DTU-WLite-S with HMS-1600-4T) — per-panel values are summed automatically as a fallback.

1.1.13.en: Added: Flow card triggers and conditions for automations (solar production started/stopped, daily summary, data updated, is solar producing). Fixed: Solar production started trigger no longer fires on every app restart. Fixed: night backoff activating at wrong hours when Homey location is not configured.

1.1.14.en: Fixed: app crash on startup when Homey location is configured — error saving coordinates to device settings was not handled correctly.

1.1.15.en: "Multilingual capability titles that follow the Homey app language. Re-pairing required to apply the new titles."

1.1.16.en: "Multilingual capability titles that follow the Homey app language. Re-pairing required to apply the new titles."

1.1.17.en: Improved DTU recovery after overnight offline periods.

1.1.18.en: Preserves the last valid daily energy value when a DTU reports zero at the end of the day, and improves diagnostics for DTU-Pro-S no-data recovery.

1.1.19.en: Improved recovery for encrypted DTU-Pro-S / DTU WLite-S devices after overnight offline periods.

1.1.20.en: Fixed night-time detection for locations west of UTC (e.g. UTC-6) where sunset falls on the next calendar day in UTC. The app now polls correctly during local daytime and only backs off during local night.

1.1.21.en: Fixed a crash during encrypted DTU recovery when Homey fails to save refreshed DTU settings such as signal strength, firmware info, or encryption metadata. Polling now continues after unexpected polling errors instead of stopping silently.

1.1.25.en: EXPERIMENTAL, contributed and tested by a user (thank you!): added support for the DTU-W100 (10D3 serial family), which rejects the standard realtime-data command but works through the legacy one — detected automatically by serial prefix, no setting to configure. Includes a longer warm-up pause after sunrise and a longer "no data" backoff tuned for this DTU's slower responses, with the same automatic connection-rebuild safety net as every other DTU (just with more patience: 2 hours instead of 20 minutes). Also fixed a bug (unrelated to the W100) where changing the Polling Interval setting had no effect until something else triggered a restart.

1.1.24.en: Fixed Lifetime Energy occasionally dropping and then jumping back up in the history — it's now rejected if fewer panels report in a poll than configured (the previous sum was incomplete, not wrong data from the device), and any other drop must repeat on the next poll before being accepted, so a one-off bad reading can't get stuck hiding real production increases from a genuinely lower value.

1.1.23.en: Raised the Panel Count limit from 8 to 32 — installations with more than 8 panels on one DTU couldn't be paired correctly, and the automatic panel-count self-correction (which runs once at startup) silently failed to fix a wrong value above 8.

1.1.22.en: Fixed a possible startup failure when encryption settings became corrupted. Improved crash resilience so a single bad panel reading no longer skips the rest of a poll update. Reduced routine log verbosity so diagnostic reports capture more useful history leading up to an issue instead of repeated status lines. Added a Fault/Alarm Detail capability that decodes the inverter's warning code into readable text instead of just an on/off alarm flag. Added two device settings, "Show per-panel voltage/current detail" and "Show AC connection voltage/current detail", to hide the per-panel and AC-connection Voltage/Current tiles if you only need the power readings — on by default, no re-pairing needed to change. Restored the repair flow (removed in v1.1.10) — fix the DTU IP address or refresh encryption settings without removing and re-adding the device. Existing devices paired before this update now get the Fault/Alarm Detail capability automatically, without re-pairing. Added a custom icon for the Fault/Alarm Detail capability. Fault/Alarm Detail now uses the official Hoymiles fault code table (264 codes, translated in 7 of our 10 languages) instead of an English-only community-sourced one, and follows Homey's active language instead of always showing English. Fixed the Fault/Alarm Detail icon not appearing on devices that already had the capability from before the icon was added, and not appearing at all even on freshly added ones — it now declares a proper default icon instead of relying only on a per-device override. Fixed Alarm/Fault Detail staying stuck on a stale warning when the DTU stops responding (e.g. at dusk) instead of clearing until it responds again.

1.1.27.en: Fixed DTUs with a 10D3 serial showing no data even though pairing read all panels: the app now tries the standard realtime-data command first and only falls back to the legacy W100 command if that returns no panels, then keeps using whichever one worked.

1.1.28.en: New device setting "Reset Daily Energy at midnight" (on by default): the DTU only resets its daily counter when production starts, so Daily Energy used to show yesterday's total all night and early in the morning. It now goes to 0 at midnight (Homey's time zone) and stays 0 until the panels produce. Uncheck it to keep the DTU's own value. Lifetime Energy and Homey Energy are not affected.

1.1.29.en: Fixed the Daily Energy midnight reset being skipped when the app or Homey restarted after midnight (e.g. after a Homey update or reboot): Daily Energy now resets correctly after a restart too.

1.1.30.en: Fixed Homey Energy counting extra solar generation in the morning: Lifetime Energy no longer drops while the panels aren't producing (dusk, night, dark weather, shade), so the real total returning the next morning is no longer counted as new production.

1.1.31.en: Daily Energy now resets at local midnight. Homey reports UTC to apps, so the app works out the time zone from your location.
